manuscript:
Reviewer A (mechanism/evidence)

Stance: a careful bounded negative empirical report, not a successful conversion method. The manuscript appropriately limits the next-message objective to the immediate linear propagation term, describes continuous recovery as an ideal diagnostic, and says lower message MSE does not establish classification gain. The residual selector is specified at useful algorithmic detail, but several definitions need tightening before readers can reproduce the method: (1) define the all-message calibration objective explicitly, including whether it is the average of six site-local losses plus a first-site message/local mixture, and distinguish it from first-message calibration; (2) state u_0 (the telescoping ReLU identity as written requires u_0=0); (3) give the precise denominator and numerator for “fraction of teacher-prediction disagreement closed”; (4) state the formula and unit of the descriptive paired 95% normal intervals. Verify the hard-event state transitions, single-node gain equation, and within-graph conjugation/permutation against source code; this review did not execute the implementation.

Novelty remains unresolved. The citations cover differential coding, adaptive calibration and graph quantization, but no systematic comparison establishes the nearest graph-specific ANN-to-SNN calibration or event-allocation work. Search primary sources and compare objective, graph operator, event budget and task; if no method novelty survives, retain the empirical-audit framing.

Reviewer B (experimental/statistical/cost scope)

Stance: credible exploratory screen; insufficient evidence for confirmatory or robust performance claims. New methods use teacher 41 and 512 fixed-index validation graphs per task. Prior exposure and lack of independent confirmation are disclosed. Because many candidate families/settings were examined on the same subset used for comparisons and the expansion decision, explicitly label results as selection-exposed and descriptive; the intervals do not address selection or multiplicity. Historical three-seed test results are baseline context only.

The strong all-position local reference is not opportunity/event matched; selector controls share the same T1-fitted base and opportunity cap. Keep these roles distinct. The cap counts possible slots, not equal nonzero events or energy. Cost reporting also needs a boundary correction: measured per-graph selector timing is not total method cost unless offline fitting/calibration/loop cost is either included or explicitly reported separately; state what fitting and preprocessing are excluded. Current RTX 3060 timing supports only higher measured diagnostic runtime for this implementation, not energy or optimized deployment cost.

Numbers cross-checked: T1 actual-message accuracy is 79.49/49.22% against strong-local references 78.13/49.41%; T2 is 0.586 pp below the same fitted base on both datasets. Immediate actual-message MSE is .002422→.001280 vs local .001378 on MNIST, and .004127→.001717 vs local .002018 on CIFAR10. The T1 CIFAR result is below strong local, and paired intervals are descriptive for one teacher.

Merged concern-to-action list

1. Major — Novelty boundary uncertain. Search/compare closest primary graph-SNN conversion and allocation work; narrow to a negative empirical audit if no distinct method claim is supported.
2. Major — Single teacher and previously exposed 512-graph validation subset, with many exploratory conditions. Explicitly label selection exposure and descriptive uncertainty; reserve confirmatory claims for independent evidence.
3. Moderate — Clarify all-message objective formula and contrast with first-site message objective; specify u_0=0 and exact disagreement-gap-closure definition.
4. Moderate — Define paired 95% normal intervals (per-graph paired correctness differences, estimator/SE, and interpretation); do not imply seed-level or confirmatory inference.
5. Moderate — State offline fitting/calibration/selection-loop cost separately from timed per-graph inference policy; clarify included and excluded operations.
6. Moderate — Distinguish strong full-position local accuracy reference from shared-base, equal-opportunity selector controls. State opportunity slots are not equal actual events/energy.
7. Moderate — Provide safe source/config/subset identities, define permutation construction, and verify event-state and gain implementation against the equations.
8. Minor — Add a concise method-family/fitting-budget map and inspect final rendered figures/tables.

No contradiction was found in the checked headline accuracies, paired deltas, message MSE or selector timing. Sampled primary-source records for Huang et al. (ICML 2025), Wang et al. (AAAI 2025) and A2Q (ICLR 2023) exist and match the cited topics; the full bibliography and novelty landscape were not audited. These are two perspectives in one native review, not independent humans.

Calibrated conclusion: continue as a bounded negative empirical manuscript; do not call it a demonstrated method advance or submission-ready.
notes: Cross-checked headline accuracies/intervals, MSE and measured selector timings against supplied CSVs; sampled three primary citation records. No code execution, source/result hash audit, full bibliography/novelty search, or rendered layout review. Offline fitting cost and several definitions need clarification. No fabricated results or consensus.
